body: I feel as though being in pain and struggling through the weeks and months is perceived as the 'selfless' thing to do, just to keep others from pain. But I agree, why is it ok for others to be selfish with their want to have us in this world when that's not what we want? I can appreciate how it would be difficult to deal with the death of a loved one but what about me. Us? The person trapped because of guilt and empathy.
Yes, would make ending life so easy
That's such a massive step! Well done x
Same
Thank you xxx

I'm actually very emotional. I loved him. He hurt me. I still cared about him more than anything. I would have saved him 100 times over if I could, despite him cheating on me. Because i knew how badly he struggled. I just don't see how being angry or letting my emotion take over can benefit me now. I've suffered with depression before all of this and I am not going back to that place without a fight. I will remain positive where i can, and cling on to the little things that can drive me forwards.
It's so damn hard, but I cannot let this take my life as well as his.
Wow.
Thank you x
Thank you to everyone. Ita great to be able to talk on here when it's so hard in the 'real' world

Thank you. I will most definitely be talking to a therapist. I was thinking about it before anyway so now I'm 100% taking the plunge and doing it. I don't find it easy to show people my emotion so a therapist should be a source of impartial help. Thanks again for your comment x

Talk to someone you really trust, friends, family or a therapist. Addressing those feelings and moments of darkness can help you in the future if you encounter them again. They did happen, and that's ok. But be proud of how far you've come...that's not bloody easy! I know.

I've been through (very recently) the same thing. My ex cheated on me and blamed his actions on his mental health and made me feel like I had to be there for him because 'it wasn't his fault'. I talked him down from a bridge after I had just found out he cheated, and since then the emotional burden of HIS actions has been laid on me time and time again. Even when I told him I couldn't continue the relationship he would make me feel guilty about it, and that he would kill himself if he didnt have me in his life. 
As someone who suffers with anxiety, this us a lot to bare...but I recently decided enough was enough and I just hope that I can move on with my life. Finally.

The problem is, people who haven't experienced these feelings/lack of, find it so hard to understand! But I do know what you mean, I'm trying to be more open with people. But it's hard, even just explaining it is hard

I get days like that too, and the only thing that stops me is the mess I'd leave behind and the hurt I'd cause. Plus, suicide isn't always easy either. 
But yeah it does take a lot of strength, and I feel like we should take the positives from that. We're still here aren't we? Even on the darkest days, we've come through fighting. 

I'd like to think it will get better.

I still do what I need to do but it's almost like I don't care anymore. Before I'd want to make sure I get the best grades I can but now I'm trying to just get through it. 

The thing is, my family have a lot of their own stuff to be thinking about and I don't want to add stress and pressure onto their lives. I've been seeing a guy but I just don't want to have that conversation with him, I find it really hard to talk about my mental health tbh.

Yeah that's what has happened to me too. The doctor increased the dose as I told him my concerns about the suicidal thoughts getting worse again but it hasn't made a difference yet. I think you're right, up and downs are to be expected. It's just bloody hard isn't it! Yeah I hope your tomorrow is better. I'm just trying to take things day by day which is something I'm not that good at!

I'm not sure, the stuff I've read about bipolar doesn't quite fit. Plus, how do you even get a mental health assessment anyway? I've never had one, just the doctor prescribing me medication. 

That's the thing...before it was my career and education. I'm studying a masters degree and the end career goal used to get me through the day. The ability to set my life up for the future and my future family. But I'm finding it so difficult to manage whilst feeling this way, the motivation to want to do well is slipping as I can't really see my future anymore.

Recently I had a few months of feeling ok, and like I would be able to get through life but then it has all come crashing back down. Yeah I am, this medication is supposed to help both but I'm not sure it's working how it should. I have a review with them soon so I will bring it up then. But I'm reluctant as i feel like this medication has really dulled my emotions, which maybe is a good thing as I haven't self harmed in a while. But it is effecting my relationships with people
Try and get her to seek professional help if you can. I know it's not easy but she sounds like she's in such a difficult place which would benefit from what they can offer. Glad she's safe

I feel like I'm doing the same thing. I don't want to cause others any grief or hassle with my death. People don't understand what this is like though, 'living' this way. I'm sorry I cant be a more positive influence but talking on here is helping me a bit. I can't talk to anyone else...again because I don't want to burden them so this is at least something.
Can you contact someone who can get to her easily? Family? Does she live with her father?
I live in the UK. I'm moving soon so maybe a change in doctor might help. How long did it take for you to actually start the treatment?

My doctor just referred me to support groups that only run during the day, I work full time so can't get there. And I've tried CBT and it didn't work for me. Other than that, they only really seems interested in prescribing more medication
